en: The Jātaka:
Catukkanipāta, Kokilavagga (The Chapter on the Cuckoo)
3. The Pakkagodha Jātaka “Even so have you been recognized by me,
O bull among charioteers, in the midst of the forest.”
For you, who carry a sword at your side,
clad in armor and wearing a tirīṭa garment,
[you stand] by the branch of an assattha tree.
“O cooked lizard, flee!
“One should associate with one who associates,
and do what is to be done for one who does what is to be done;”
One should not do what is beneficial for one who does not desire benefit;
nor should one associate with one who does not associate.
One should abandon one who abandons, and one should not harbor attachment.
One whose heart has departed should not associate with them;
like a bird that, knowing a tree’s fruit is exhausted,
seeks another, so too should one look elsewhere, for the world is vast.
“Therefore, I shall do for you according to my power,
O Kṣatriya, out of regard for your gratitude;
and I grant you all sovereignty.”
“I shall give it to you for whatever you desire.
This concludes the third Jātaka, the Pakkagodha Jātaka.
